This document describes a vocabulary, in this case OSLO Mobility - Timetable and Planning (Vocabulary). A vocabulary is a collection of reusable terms, namely classes and properties, whose meaning is recorded through a label and definition. For terms defined in this domain, additional formal agreements are available. For external terms, the formal agreements are copied from the external source.

Summary

This vocabulary contains the terms necessary to describe the timetable and planning of public transport networks.

The terminology is based on EPIP, which is a profile on NETEX that allows, among other things, to describe time tables and stops. The terms that can be used to describe vehicle planning are based on NETEX only.

To describe time tables, we must first be able to describe the public transport offer by means of Networks, Lines and the Routes they follow.

To describe the network topology, we have Ride Patterns that indicate how the Routes run correctly by means of Points.

Patterns of loaded Journeys (the so-called Service Journeys) run along Planned Stops, these are the logical stops of the Network: places from which one can travel to other stops or where one can change to other Lines.

For the Points through which the Journeys pass (including the Scheduled Stops), Transit Times can be described, either the times along the stops of a Line (in a certain direction) or all Transit times during the day at a stop.

It is possible to diversify Service Trips by day type (weekday, school day, etc.) and to link them to actual dates in order to have a Service Calendar for a certain school year, for example.

The Planned Stopping Points are logical stops, but it is common for them to coincide spatially (within walking distance of each other) and to be part of one large physical stop (the Stop), e.g. a train station.

It is possible to describe a hierarchy of Stops (Multimodal, Unimodal, Platform). More detail can also be given about the infrastructure of the physical stop, e.g. the entrances and exits.

There is also terminology in this vocabulary to describe so-called Blocks. This is an important concept when planning the service provided by the public transport company. They are fixed sequences of Trips, intended to use the vehicles (and therefore the drivers) as efficiently as possible.

These can be linked to the most suitable Vehicle types (e.g. based on their Passenger capacity) and to the Service Calendar to easily assign drivers to Blocks.

Status of this document

This section describes the status of this document at the time of publication. It is possible that newer versions have already been released in the meantime.

This vocabulary has the status Erkende Standaard and was issued on 2022-04-21.

This document is an official specification of a vocabulary and provides a shared conceptual framework for certain concepts. This specification serves to clarify the definition, use, domain, and scope of the RDF terms within this domain. The terms defined in this vocabulary are persistent and will therefore never disappear, nor will the definitions change except to further clarify an existing definition. However, terms may be labeled as obsolete and replaced in newer versions of this specification.

1. License

This specification of Informatie Vlaanderen is published under the "Model License Free Reuse - v1.0".

2. Conformity

An exchange of data, by whatever means, is subject to this vocabulary when it uses the terminology (classes and properties) in a manner consistent with the semantics established in the latest version of the specification (domain, scope, definition and usage) and does not use terminology from other vocabularies as an alternative to the proposed terminology included in this vocabulary.

Service Journey Links allow Route Planners to more easily calculate the shortest Routes.

6. External terminology

Since 2025, external terms are no longer included as non-normative mapping in vocabularies of data.vlaanderen.be.

Instead, a table with which external URIs are used has been added to each application profile. This simplifies the objective of this document. Namely listing and managing terms defined in this namespace.

To still achieve harmonization of the use of external terminology, a general mapping is published.
